docs.text:
This is the official StarPilot wiki for installation, supported hardware, features, and troubleshooting.

StarPilot is a standalone, community-driven openpilot fork for comma 3, 3X, and 4. It adds driving options, Galaxy device management, and vehicle support.

docs.title: StarPilot FAQ and Troubleshooting
docs.text: Can't find an answer to your question? Post in Discord or submit feedback through the ticket system.

docs.title: How do I submit feedback?
docs.text:
Important

StarPilot thrives on the feedback and responsiveness of our community. If you are experiencing an issue, please open a ticket and share what you are seeing. The more people submitting feedback, the better your car (and everyone else's) can drive.

Use the StarPilot ticket system to report bugs, share tuning feedback, request features, or ask for an issue to be investigated. The guide explains which button to choose and what information to include.

docs.title: What is StarPilot?
docs.text: StarPilot is a standalone, community-driven fork of openpilot. It runs on comma 3, 3X, and 4 and adds driving, device management, and customization features. See the StarPilot overview and installation guide.

docs.title: What is the Galaxy? Can I change settings from my phone?
docs.text: Galaxy lets you manage StarPilot from a browser on the same local network, or remotely after pairing. Local access works without Internet. Remote access requires Internet. See Companion Apps for iOS and Android.

docs.title: Does StarPilot support Comma 3, 3X, and 4?
docs.text: Yes. StarPilot supports comma 3, 3X and 4, including continued support for older devices. Feature availability depends on the device, vehicle and configuration. See Comma Devices for details.

docs.title: Does StarPilot support Chestnut (external GPU)?
docs.text: Yes. You can download compatible GPU models before connecting Chestnut. Running them requires ready, supported hardware. Most users do not need Chestnut. See Chestnut and Models.

docs.title: Why is my car driving terribly?
docs.text:
If a custom setting may be contributing, try Safe Mode. It temporarily bypasses supported custom features and tuning without erasing their saved settings. To restore default toggle values, back up your settings first and follow Backup and reset.

If the behavior persists, include your vehicle, hardware, software version and route details in a support ticket.

docs.title: Will installing openpilot void my warranty?
docs.text: https://comma.ai/support#will-installing-a-comma-device-void-my-warranty

docs.title: Is the openpilot install reversible?
docs.text: A standard plug-in harness installation can generally be removed. Firmware flashing and hardware retrofits may require separate restoration. See the Volt firmware guidance for an example.

docs.title: Will openpilot navigate on its own?
docs.text: StarPilot is driver assistance. Stay attentive and ready to take control. Navigation & Maps can provide guidance for supported low-speed turns with the matching turn signal on and blind spot clear. It can also request slowing for an upcoming maneuver when StarPilot controls speed. See Operation for driving behavior.

docs.title: How do I clear the "LKAS Fault: Restart the car" error?
docs.text: Pull over safely and turn the vehicle off. Follow the fault recovery guidance for your vehicle. If the fault recurs, report the exact configuration and include the route or logs.

docs.title: How do I avoid LKAS faults?
docs.text: Switch the vehicle off before rebooting, unplugging or turning off the comma. Interrupting the connection while the vehicle is on can cause an LKAS fault.

docs.title: How do I clear the "Cruise Fault: Restart the car" error?
docs.text: Park safely and turn the vehicle off before following the restart guidance for your vehicle. If the fault persists, include the hardware, software version and route details in a support ticket.

docs.title: How do I clear the "Controls Mismatch" error?
docs.text: Park and switch the vehicle off before restarting the comma. If the error persists, report your exact vehicle configuration, how you started the car and the matching route or log.

docs.title: How do I upload logs for troubleshooting?
docs.text:
Logs are sent as routes. A route is a single drive (from car on to car off), with one-minute segments. Log data can include video, vehicle messages and GPS. If support accepts a local export, use Routes in Galaxy to download the recording or logs. Downloading them does not upload anything to comma Connect.

  1. Navigate to connect.comma.ai
  2. Find the route your issue happened on and click on it.
  3. Click and drag the video slider over the section where the error happened. The video will loop over this selected section, make sure the error is within. To undo your last selection, click the back arrow just above the video slider. Once you are happy with the segments selected, proceed to the next step.
  4. Click Files, then next to All logs, click (upload ## logs)
  5. Wait for data to be uploaded (you can check the progress using Files > View Upload Queue)
  6. If you choose to share the route publicly, open More info, enable Public access and copy the route information. Turn public access off when sharing is no longer needed.
  7. Create a ticket using the buttons in the #submit-feedback-and-reports channel of the Discord server. Be as descriptive as possible. Also include the approximate minute(s) in the route it happened. StarPilot has a unique, community-focused ticketing system that helps users and developers make sure no problem goes unresolved. Learn how it works and what to include in your report.

Tip

Ending a route log early While safely parked, open Settings → System → Force Drive State → Offroad on the comma to stop driving services and end the route. In Galaxy, the equivalent control is Tools → System Tools → Software & Updates → Advanced options → Force device offroad. Return the comma to Auto, or turn off Force device offroad in Galaxy, when you are done.

docs.title: I'm stuck on the boot logo screen. How do I fix it?
docs.text:
If Galaxy is reachable, try the backup and reset tools. Save any recordings or logs you need before resetting the device.

If Galaxy is unavailable, follow If You Cannot Open Settings for your device. A factory reset erases stored content and settings. If the problem persists, ask in Discord.

docs.title: My device is behaving oddly. What is a "saveme"?
docs.text: For a settings problem, open Backup and reset in Galaxy. Use Back up toggles first. You can then Restore toggles from a compatible backup, or use Reset toggles to default while parked. The toggle reset keeps your recordings and other device data.

docs.title: How do I fix the "CAN bus disconnected" Error?
docs.text: With the vehicle off, inspect and reseat connections according to the hardware guide for your setup. Check the harness, OBD-C cable and pedal connection where applicable. If the error persists, ask for support with your vehicle, hardware and logs.

docs.title: Ticket System
docs.text:
StarPilot thrives on the feedback and responsiveness of our community. If you are experiencing an issue, please open a ticket and share what you are seeing. The more people submitting feedback, the better your car (and everyone else's) can drive.

For a StarPilot BT connection or app issue on iPhone, use Submit logs through Discord in the app. Some Galaxy Android builds also offer Discord reporting.

docs.title: What is it?
docs.text: The Discord ticket system is the main way to report problems and request support for StarPilot. Create a ticket if your car meets Comma's requirements but is not yet supported by StarPilot, if you experience ping-ponging or steering wobble, or if you encounter another issue that requires investigation. For basic configuration questions, ask in the appropriate public support channel instead. Firestar will review your ticket when available and may release an update to address the issue.

docs.title: Before creating a ticket!
docs.text:
You must first be a member of the StarPilot Discord server.

Potential fixes are first released on the testing branch. If you are using the stable branch, you will need to switch to testing to test the update.

docs.title: How do I create a ticket?
docs.text:
1. Open the StarPilot Discord.
  2. Go to the #submit-feedback-and-reports channel.

  3. Select the appropriate report button.

  4. Fill out the form, then select Submit. For an issue, include:

    • Your comma device, vehicle year and trim, and installed hardware
    • The branch and software version you tested
    • The approximate time, route or bookmark, and any relevant logs
    • What you expected and what actually happened

    Choose whether to make a route public before sharing it.

docs.title: Which button should I choose?
docs.text:
Bug Report Use Bug Report when something is not working correctly. For example, use it if a steering-wheel button no longer works as expected. Feedback Use Feedback for non-urgent tuning concerns, such as insufficient steering performance or steering wobble. Feature Request Use Feature Request to suggest a new StarPilot feature. If you request a feature, be prepared to test it. View My Reports Use View My Reports to see a list of your reports and their current status.

Tip

If you can reproduce the issue, open a bookmark on your device shortly before it occurs and close the bookmark shortly afterward. Include the bookmark information in your ticket to help Firestar locate and investigate the issue.

docs.title: How do I switch from stable to testing?
docs.text: Park and turn off the vehicle. Keep the comma powered and online, then follow Changing branches and choose Testing in Galaxy. You can switch without reinstalling StarPilot. Once the fix is in Stable, follow the same steps and choose Stable to switch back.

docs.title: What do the colored circles on my ticket mean?
docs.text:
Each colored circle represents the current status of your ticket.

Color Meaning What you should do 🟠 Your ticket is new and has been submitted. Wait for Firestar to review it. ⚪ Firestar has reviewed your ticket, but an update is not ready yet. The circle will turn purple when the update is ready to test. Please be patient and wait for the circle to turn purple. 🟣 Your ticket has been reviewed and a potential fix is ready. Update to the requested testing build and test the fix. If the problem remains, submit a new route and updated logs. 🔴 Your ticket was sent back for further investigation. Wait for the ticket to return to purple status. 🟢 You closed the ticket yourself. No further action is required. 🔵 A staff member or the bot closed your ticket. No further action is required.

docs.title: Pedestrian alert troubleshooting
docs.text:
If your car displays a pedestrian alert warning, check the owner’s manual for the exact dashboard message. Use the service guidance for your vehicle’s model year and configuration before changing any fuse or wiring.

If the warning appeared after installing StarPilot hardware, ask for support with the vehicle year and trim, installed hardware, exact warning and when it appeared.

docs.title: Vehicle Quirks
docs.text:
Things to be aware of for your vehicle:

  • Steering assistance has a minimum operating speed. Be ready to steer at low speeds.
  • On supported non-ACC Bolts, the Comma Pedal uses regen in one-pedal or L mode to slow the vehicle. Braking can be limited, especially at low speed. Be ready to brake manually.
  • On supported ACC Bolts, StarPilot can request friction braking through the factory ACC system. A compatible pedal can add stronger regen and support restarting from a stop. See ACC Bolts.
  • The regen paddle can disengage assistance where supported. If the LKAS button is unavailable with the harness connected, some ACC configurations can still use the distance button for supported actions.

docs.title: StarPilot Settings
docs.text: In Galaxy, open Toggles → Vehicle. Use Auto or select the exact registered vehicle configuration if manual identification is needed. With the vehicle off, verify the ACC, harness and pedal options for your setup before your next drive. See Settings for supported controller choices.

docs.title: Tires
docs.text:
• Use the pressures recommended for your vehicle and tires.
  • Keep your car aligned.
  • Check the vehicle manufacturer’s guidance before changing wheel or tire sizes.

docs.title: One Pedal Driving/L Mode
docs.text: On Bolt setups that use the Comma Pedal for regen braking, use One Pedal mode on Gen 2 or L mode on Gen 0 and Gen 1. Factory ACC and ACC-plus-pedal configurations have their own braking behavior.

docs.title: Sport Mode
docs.text: On affected 2022–23 Bolts, Sport Mode can reduce available steering torque. Leave it off if it affects steering response.

docs.title: Should I buy a Comma Pedal?
docs.text: Our recommendation for whether or not to purchase the pedal depends on if your car is ACC or Non-ACC.

docs.title: Non-ACC Bolts
docs.text:
On supported non-ACC Bolts, the Comma Pedal is strongly recommended. It lets StarPilot accelerate and use regen braking in One Pedal or L mode. Braking and restarting from a stop depend on the vehicle and pedal setup.

Without the pedal, supported configurations use CC Long, also called Redneck ACC to adjust factory cruise. The Bolt CC Long profiles require at least 24 mph to engage. Be ready to brake manually.

docs.title: ACC Bolts
docs.text:
On supported ACC Bolts, StarPilot can use ACC commands for gas and friction braking. Without a pedal, you may need to use the accelerator or cruise resume to move again from a stop.

A compatible Comma Pedal is optional. Supported ACC-plus-pedal configurations can blend pedal-based regen with ACC friction braking and can support stop-and-go. Confirm the setup for your vehicle before ordering hardware.

Your Bolt may have had a momentary issue communicating with the throttle pedal.

With the vehicle off, inspect and reseat the pedal connections using the hardware supplier’s instructions. If propulsion or pedal faults remain, stop using the setup and ask for help.

docs.text: This guide covers specific configurations of the Hyundai Ioniq 6 HDA II, Kia EV9 HDA II and Hyundai Ioniq 5 PE with HDA II and LFA2. Check Vehicle Compatibility for the applicable model and configuration.

docs.title: First-Time Things to Toggle
docs.text: In Galaxy, open Toggles → Vehicle. Verify the recognized model and use the exact registered configuration if manual selection is needed. On setups where openpilot Longitudinal Control (Alpha) is available, follow the Openpilot Toggles guidance before enabling it. Availability depends on the vehicle and configuration.

docs.title: Startup by vehicle
docs.text:
Startup checks differ by vehicle. Use the startup instructions confirmed for your exact vehicle and control configuration.

On an Ioniq 5 PE with HDA II and LFA2, the vehicle can retain factory speed control when takeover is unavailable.

A cruise or HDA indicator on the dashboard does not by itself confirm that StarPilot is controlling speed. If you're unsure how to confirm the handoff or a startup check fails, leave the controls disengaged and ask in Discord with your vehicle, hardware, software version and what you saw at startup.

docs.title: Engaging speed control
docs.text: Use the controls for your vehicle. Depending on the configuration, steering and speed control can engage separately. Use the applicable SET, RES and Cancel controls as described in Operation. SET adjustments can differ between factory cruise and StarPilot speed control. See Wheel Controls.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Verify the recognized vehicle and check the displayed availability or startup status. If the openpilot Longitudinal Control (Alpha) control is unavailable for your configuration, keep factory cruise settings. Switch the vehicle off before restarting the comma. If the expected handoff is still unavailable, include the startup status and route details in a support ticket.

docs.title: Vehicle Compatibility
docs.text:
StarPilot adds support for cars that stock openpilot doesn't cover, and re-tunes a number of cars that are supported by stock so they drive better.

Support depends on your car’s model year, trim, region, steering system, ACC configuration, and installed hardware. Check the requirements for your exact configuration before choosing hardware or enabling controls.

Trim, package, and harness notes describe specific configurations. Check the car guide or ask in Discord about other setups.

docs.title: Vehicle tuning improvements
docs.text:
StarPilot includes vehicle-specific tuning and optional control settings. Available changes depend on the vehicle, steering system, speed-control configuration and selected controller.

  • Hyundai / Kia / Genesis — Acceleration changes depend on the vehicle and whether StarPilot controls speed.
  • Honda / Acura — Stopping behavior depends on the speed-control configuration.
  • Toyota — Lateral tuning refinements are available on supported torque-steering setups.
  • GM — Braking and regen behavior depend on the ACC, pedal and retrofit configuration.

Some configurations retain their standard controller settings. Optional StarPilot controllers and vehicle-specific features can change behavior where supported.

docs.title: Required Hardware - Volt & Other ASCM/SDGM Cars
docs.text:
The Volt has a number of possible configurations. This page lists hardware and control options for common configurations. Match the vehicle, harness and speed-control setup before ordering parts.

There are two parts to OpenPilot control: Lateral Control (Steering) & Longitudinal Control (Gas/Brake).

On supported ASCM and SDGM setups, the harness can provide steering while the factory ACC keeps speed control. A compatible SASCM setup can allow StarPilot to control speed. If you plan to keep factory ACC, follow the steering-only hardware requirements for your car.

docs.text:

  • 2019 Chevy Volt with Factory ACC: SDGM Harness & SASCM
  • Volts without Factory ACC: Volts without ACC
  • Non-Volt Car with ASCM: ASCM Harness & SASCM
  • Non-Volt Car with SDGM: SDGM Harness & SASCM

Tip

We recommend purchasing from BearTechWorkshop (aka tinybear) whenever possible. They are a small business providing the openpilot community with high quality products and excellent customer support.

Parked power

Power requirements differ by harness. Follow your car’s hardware guide. SDGM requires the correct OBD power connection. Parked runtime depends on available power, the shutdown timer and the battery-voltage cutoff.

docs.title: Cameras & Monitoring
docs.text:
In Galaxy, Cameras & Monitoring contains the blind spot camera preview (PiP), Sentry, V-ASM spot monitoring, and a camera snapshot tool. Configure them while parked. For road-camera speed sign detection, see Vision speed limits.

See this in Galaxy: camera tools

Open Tools → Cameras & Monitoring to find the separate PiP, Sentry, and V-ASM pages.

The snapshot tool starts without an image. PiP and V-ASM have separate setup pages; no camera snapshot was taken for this example. Tap the image to open it full size.

docs.title: Camera Snapshot
docs.text:
On the main Cameras & Monitoring page, turn off the vehicle, choose Cabin, Wide road, or Road, then tap Take snapshot. Use Clear to remove the preview. These snapshots are temporary and are not saved as Sentry events.

Use Galaxy in a browser over a local network or through your signed-in remote link. Camera images require a network connection.

docs.title: V-ASM: adjacent spot monitoring
docs.text:
V-ASM adds visual spot warnings alongside factory blind spot monitoring, where available. It does not confirm that a lane is clear or change vehicle controls. Always check mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

Why the window regions are required: The cabin camera also sees the driver, pillars, and interior. V-ASM uses each region to crop and mask the matching side-window view before checking it for a vehicle. This tells the model which side to inspect and keeps unrelated parts of the image out of its input. At least one side must be marked before monitoring can be enabled; mark both sides if you want warnings on both.

  1. In Galaxy, open Cameras & Monitoring → V-ASM while parked. Tap Take new snapshot to load the cabin camera image.
  2. Select Left or Right for the vehicle side you want to mark. The preview is mirrored, so the vehicle's left appears on the left; Galaxy stores it as camera right. The vehicle's right appears on the right and is stored as camera left.
  3. Tap around the visible side glass for that side, then repeat for the other side. Include the front and rear side windows and as much visible glass as practical. Leave out pillars, door frames, and interior; include a side mirror if visible through the glass. A B-pillar can be inside a continuous region if needed. Use Undo or Clear to fix points. Each region needs at least three points.
  4. Tap Save, review the region, and confirm. Then turn on Use visual spot monitoring under the saved settings. A drawn region by itself does not enable warnings.

Detection confidence sets how strong the model's evidence must be (0.80–1.00). Raising it may reduce false alerts but miss vehicles. Warning smoothing (0.01–0.50 seconds) controls how quickly warnings change; raising it reduces flicker but delays changes. Start with the defaults and adjust only if you notice a problem. Changes to these settings require the vehicle to be parked.

The cabin snapshot stays in your browser and is not uploaded by the region editor. If a warning is missing or incorrect, you can submit an edge case or read about the training data.

docs.title: PiP: blind spot camera preview
docs.text:
Blind Spot Camera and Preview shows a close-up of a cabin side window on the driving screen. It can appear when you signal, when the car reports a blind spot warning, or when V-ASM reports a visual spot warning. It is a view for the driver, not a second detection model.

In Galaxy, open Cameras & Monitoring → Blind Spot Camera and Preview while parked. Take a cabin snapshot, choose Left camera or Right camera, and place its circular crop over the matching side window. Adjust Crop size, then Save and confirm. Turn on Use blind spot camera and choose Show on turn signal, Show on blind spot warning, or both. The warning option responds to factory blind spot warnings and to V-ASM warnings when V-ASM is configured and enabled. Select Position side cameras to open the layout editor and place the previews on the driving screen.

PiP's circular crop controls what appears on screen. V-ASM's window regions control what its model analyzes; configure them separately. PiP also needs a live cabin camera and a crop for the side being shown.

docs.title: Sentry: parked motion events
docs.text: Open Cameras & Monitoring → Sentry for parked motion monitoring, saved events, and notifications. See the Sentry Mode guide for setup and event details.

docs.title: Lane Centering
docs.text:
Lane Centering is a StarPilot feature that helps keep your vehicle centered between detected lane lines while still allowing the End-to-End (E2E) model to control the driving path.

Instead of replacing the E2E model, Lane Centering works alongside it.

docs.title: How Does Lane Centering Work?
docs.text:
When both lane lines are detected clearly and confidently, StarPilot compares the E2E model's predicted path with the center of the lane.

If they differ, StarPilot applies a small, smooth correction toward the lane center while still allowing the E2E model to make driving decisions.

With one reliable lane line, StarPilot can sometimes adjust the model path to maintain clearance using other reliable geometry, such as a road edge. If neither path correction has enough evidence, or a lane change or another condition prevents correction, StarPilot falls back to the normal E2E path.

docs.title: How Can I Tell Which Direction Lane Centering Is Correcting?
docs.text: The lane line on the side StarPilot is pulling toward can change color when a correction is active. The indicator depends on the driving display and your color settings.

docs.title: How Do I Enable Lane Centering?
docs.text:
In Galaxy, open Toggles → Lateral (Steering) → Lane Centering. You can also search for Lane Centering in Toggles. Availability depends on the vehicle and configuration.

See this in Galaxy: lane-centering controls

Open Toggles → Lateral (Steering) → Lane Centering to find the enable switch, pause behavior, lane offset, and model path preference.

This cropped view shows the first controls. Values are examples, not recommended settings; available controls and scales can vary by version. Tap the image to open it full size.

docs.title: Lane offset
docs.text: Lane offset lets you adjust the preferred position within the lane, for example slightly closer to the right side.

docs.title: Model path preference
docs.text: Higher Model path preference lets a confident model path reduce the centering correction when it differs from the lane center.

docs.title: Lane Centering Strength
docs.text: Lane Centering Strength adjusts the amount of correction. Use 100% for the normal correction. Lower values reduce it and higher values strengthen it.

docs.title: Pause on signal
docs.text:
Pause on signal temporarily pauses the centering correction when the turn signal is active.

Important

Lane Centering works alongside the driving model and falls back to its normal path when required conditions aren’t met.

docs.title: Navigation & Maps
docs.text: Galaxy sends a destination to your comma and shows route choices. Steering and speed follow your normal engagement settings.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
While parked, open Galaxy → Tools → Navigation & Maps → Setup. Turn on Navigation and save a public Mapbox token, starting with pk..

An optional Google key adds Google maps, traffic-aware routing and place search. Mapbox remains required.

See this in Galaxy: navigation setup

Open Tools → Navigation & Maps → Setup. This is where you find the Navigation switch and route preferences.

The setup view is cropped before the key sections. Source badges and preferences are examples; use the written setup instructions for required keys. Tap the image to open it full size.

docs.title: Plan a route
docs.text:
On Destination, search for a place or choose a saved or recent one. Tap a result to start guidance and choose an alternate route if offered. Change destination searches again; End navigation clears the route. The star saves a place as Home, Work or another favorite.

Routes show traffic-aware choices and ETA when available. Galaxy can reroute after a route deviation. You can start or end guidance through your remote Galaxy link.

docs.title: Position / GPS
docs.text:
Under Setup → Position, choose:

  • Comma and car, phone as backup: uses phone GPS when neither comma nor car has a fix.
  • Comma and car only: does not use phone GPS.
  • Phone first: uses a recent phone fix, otherwise comma or car GPS.

Enable location sharing in a supported companion app to supply phone GPS. Updates reach the comma over Bluetooth or local Wi-Fi.

docs.title: Offline Maps
docs.text:
Offline Map Management saves Mapbox road lines for the map overlay. Downloads use Wi-Fi and require your Mapbox key. Google map tiles cannot be saved offline.

Speed Limit Maps downloads regional coverage for map-based speed limits. The selected coverage applies the next time the Maps service starts. Choose Maps as a source in the Speed Limit Controller to use those readings.

Planning a new route still needs Internet.

docs.title: How it helps while driving
docs.text:
Galaxy manages destinations and saved places; the comma displays turn-by-turn instructions.

Turn assistance is limited to supported low-speed turns with the matching turn signal and corresponding blindspot clear. Upcoming maneuvers can also reduce the target speed when StarPilot controls speed.

Navigation does not complete turns or exits for you. Stay attentive and ready to steer or brake.

docs.title: Sentry Mode
docs.text: Sentry Mode captures events when the comma detects sustained movement while your car is parked. Set up monitoring and review events through Galaxy.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Sentry uses your comma device's accelerometer to detect movement while the vehicle is parked, for example if someone bumps or rocks it.

With monitoring enabled, the vehicle off and sufficient power, Sentry arms after 90 seconds of continuous valid conditions. If those conditions are interrupted, it may need to arm again. Motion can create a warning, and further activity can escalate to an alarm.

The comma’s normal parked shutdown and battery cutoff still apply.

docs.title: Galaxy dashboard
docs.text:
Open Cameras & Monitoring → Sentry to turn monitoring on or off, adjust its settings and review events. The event list refreshes while the page is open. Select Delete to remove an event or Delete All to clear the list.

For a live parked image, use Camera Snapshot.

See this in Galaxy: parked motion settings

Open Cameras & Monitoring → Sentry. The status appears above the monitoring switch, sensitivity, and warning persistence.

This example is disarmed. Values shown are not recommendations. Notifications and event images are outside this view. Tap the image to open it full size.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
The Sentry page supports Browser push, Discord, General webhook, ntfy and Galaxy App Alerts where available. Browser push requires HTTPS and a compatible browser. App alerts require permission on the phone and a configured push relay. Use the test button for each channel you set up.

iPhone users

Add Galaxy to your Home Screen as a web app before enabling browser notifications. iOS requires a Home Screen web app for web push to work.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting What it does Use parked motion monitoring Turn parked monitoring on or off Motion sensitivity How easily movement triggers Sentry. Lower values catch smaller bumps; higher values require stronger motion Warning persistence How much motion evidence triggers the first warning. Higher values help filter brief vibrations.

Start with the defaults and adjust sensitivity if you get too many false alerts or not enough real ones.

docs.title: What gets captured
docs.text:
Galaxy lists Motion, Alarm, Selfie and Low battery events with timestamps. Motion and alarm events can include road and cabin images when the capture succeeds. Low battery entries show the measured battery voltage and the cutoff.

Sentry stores up to 512 events. When storage is full, new events can’t be saved until you clear space. Use a supported network connection to view event images. Bluetooth-only access can show event details.

docs.title: Speed Limit Controller
docs.text:
The Speed Limit Controller, or SLC, uses the accepted speed limit plus a configurable offset. SET is your cruise ceiling. SLC can cap the target below SET. Accepting a posted limit normally leaves SET where it is.

SLC does not replace the driver's judgment. Speed-limit information can be missing, delayed, or incorrect. Always follow posted signs and adjust the set speed when needed.

docs.title: Enable SLC
docs.text:
In Galaxy, open Toggles → Longitudinal (Speed & Following) → Speed Limit Controller. Show speed limit signs displays available readings. For accepted limits to affect cruise speed, enable Speed Limit Controller on a supported configuration where StarPilot controls speed.

See this in Galaxy: speed-limit controls

Open Toggles → Longitudinal (Speed & Following) → Speed Limit Controller. The controller and sign-display switches are separate controls.

Disabled controls can depend on your vehicle or other settings. The values shown are an example, not recommended settings. Tap the image to open it full size.

docs.title: Driving-screen colors
docs.text: The speed-limit sign displays the limit and indicates when a new reading needs confirmation. A green outline indicates active limiting where shown. OVERRIDE indicates that an override is active. The cruise SET display still shows the driver’s ceiling.

docs.title: Speed-limit sources
docs.text:
SLC can use the following sources:

  • Dashboard reads a speed limit supplied by a supported vehicle.
  • Maps uses installed Speed Limit Maps for the current road.
  • Vision uses the road camera to detect speed-limit signs.

Use Primary source, Secondary source and Third source to choose the order. SLC tries the next configured source when the first cannot provide a usable reading.

Choose Highest or Lowest as the primary source to compare usable Dashboard and Maps readings by value. Usable Vision readings are included when Vision is selected as the secondary or third source.

docs.title: Vision speed limits
docs.text: Choose Vision in any of the three source fields where available. Check camera-reported limits against road signs. Vision can misread signs, so keep another source available and use Confirm limits when evaluating it. To help improve detection, see Vision Speed Limit Detection.

docs.title: Configure speed offsets
docs.text:
The offset editor lets you set a separate adjustment for each of seven posted-speed bands. Use the bands and units shown in Galaxy. A positive offset raises the adjusted limit and a negative offset lowers it.

For example, with SET at 65 mph and an accepted limit of 50 mph plus a 5 mph offset, SLC caps the target at 55 mph. SET stays at 65 mph.

docs.title: Confirm new speed limits
docs.text:
Use Confirm limits to choose Off, Both, Higher only or Lower only. Off adopts new readings automatically.

When a prompt is active, press + to accept or − to decline within 30 seconds. You can also tap the sign to open the decision controls. A prompt that times out leaves the new limit unaccepted.

docs.title: Look ahead for changes
docs.text: Use Adopt higher limits early and Adopt lower limits early for upcoming changes in map data. Each setting can be Off or set to 1–10 seconds. Lookahead depends on available map data.

docs.title: Match the limit when engaging
docs.text: Match speed limit on engage can initialize SET to the adjusted speed limit when you engage. Use RES to restore the previous SET speed where supported. An ordinary limit accepted later still caps the target below SET without changing it.

docs.title: When a reading is unavailable
docs.text: If fresh readings are unavailable, an already accepted limit can remain in effect, bounded by SET. If there is no accepted limit, ordinary SET behavior applies.

docs.title: Override SLC
docs.text:
Use After an accelerator override to choose what happens when you release the accelerator:

  • Resume the adjusted limit returns to the adjusted speed limit.
  • Hold the speed you reached keeps the speed you reached, bounded by SET.
  • Use your SET speed lets SET govern the target.

On supported configurations, Override speed limit with + lets the cruise increase button raise SET past the adjusted limit and bypass the cap. When a confirmation prompt is active, + accepts the proposed limit. The posted reading stays the same when you override the cap.

docs.title: Show source information
docs.text: Where available, enable the source display options to compare readings from the dashboard, maps and Vision. A source value is a reading. The accepted limit and its offset are the values SLC uses to cap your target.

docs.title: Incorrect or missing map limits
docs.text:
Map-based speed limits come from OpenStreetMap. If a road has an incorrect or missing limit, correct it in OpenStreetMap. When newer coverage is available, download it for your region in Speed Limit Maps. The updated coverage is selected for the next Maps service start.

See Vision Speed Limit Detection if you want to help improve camera-based sign detection.

Start conservatively

Start with confirmation enabled and small offsets. Display the source information while testing so you can see where each limit came from. Change one setting at a time and verify its behavior before relying on it regularly.

docs.title: StarPort
docs.text: Open Galaxy → Tools → StarPort while parked. StarPort shows StarPilot on your car screen or tablet. Choose built-in wireless Android Auto, a wireless adapter, USB where available, or a tablet app. Tested adapters include AAWireless and Motorola MA1. The supported tablet apps are HeadunitPad on iPad and Open Headunit on Android tablets.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
See this in Galaxy: StarPort support status

Open Tools → StarPort. Check StarPort Support before following the connection steps below.

This example already has support installed. Your status and validity date may differ. The view is cropped before paired-device details. Tap the image to open it full size.

docs.title: StarPort Support
docs.text: Under StarPort Support, choose Install support. Follow Galaxy’s download instructions for a stable Android Auto package by Google LLC. Use Choose File to select the package as downloaded, then choose Install or Turn On and Install. Wait for Ready. For wireless car or adapter pairing, enable Bluetooth if Galaxy prompts you. Use a local network connection for the package download and upload.

docs.title: Connection choices
docs.text:
Choose What to do Built-in wireless Open the car’s phone pairing screen. Tap Find car, select the car and confirm the code on both screens. Wireless adapter Use the car’s wired Android Auto data port. Select Wireless adapter in StarPort and follow the adapter pairing steps. USB cable If Wired AA is available, connect the car’s Android Auto USB data port to the comma with a data-capable cable. Tablet app Put the tablet on the same Wi-Fi as the comma or join the Galaxy hotspot. Follow the steps Galaxy shows for the selected app.

Tap Connect when prompted. Keep the car on and its screen awake for the first connection. Enable Automatic Connection to connect when you start driving.

Disconnect wired Android Auto before enabling Jetlink. Both use the comma's USB-C port.

docs.title: Pair a wireless adapter
docs.text:
1. Verify wired Android Auto works in the car’s USB data port, then plug the adapter into that port. In StarPort, select Wireless adapter and choose the matching adapter model.
  2. If an old phone is already using the adapter, disconnect it or temporarily turn off that phone’s Bluetooth and Wi-Fi. Leave the adapter powered.
  3. Open pairing mode on the adapter. On an AAWireless TWO, hold the button for about two seconds until the light is solid purple. Look for AAWireless-XXXX. For another AAWireless model, follow its model-specific pairing steps. On a Motorola MA1, hold the button and release as soon as the light flashes blue. Look for AndroidAuto-XXXX.
  4. Tap Find adapter, or Pair another adapter if one is already selected. If more than one device appears, match the advertised name and suffix to yours. Select it and follow the pairing prompts. Use the adapter entry for this connection. If Galaxy asks you to connect a paired car in Bluetooth, do that and return to StarPort.
  5. If discovery or pairing times out, confirm the adapter is still in pairing mode and the old phone is disconnected. Restart discovery. If the adapter keeps hanging up, briefly unplug it and reconnect it while the car screen stays on. For a stale pairing, follow Start over.

AAWireless pairing guide · Motorola MA1 user guide

docs.title: Connection problems
docs.text:
What Galaxy shows What to check Finding Android Auto or Waiting for car Wi-Fi Check that StarPort Support shows Ready, the right car or adapter is selected, and wireless Android Auto is enabled in the car. Waiting for your USB cable Use the car’s Android Auto data port and a data-capable cable. Connected · car screen in use Open Android Auto on the car screen to return to StarPilot. Trying your connection again Let StarPort retry and follow the prompts.

If the screen is black or frozen, tap Disconnect, wait a few seconds, then reconnect. If it keeps happening, restart the car or adapter.

docs.title: Connection Logs
docs.text:
1. Try to reproduce the issue while parked. Open Connection Logs in StarPort and find the attempt by time, car and connection type. The list shows up to 20 sessions, newest first.
  2. Check the outcome. Projected means the connection reached the projection stage. Failed shows the recorded error. A stop at RFCOMM means the attempt ended during Bluetooth setup. Include the last status shown in Galaxy if the log gives little detail.
  3. For a StarPort issue, use Send StarPort logs if it is available. Add a short description of what happened. You can also use Download all logs over a network connection and attach the zip to a support ticket. Include the car year/model, adapter model, connection type and steps you tried. Bluetooth-only access shows summaries and can send the archive from the comma when Send StarPort logs is available.

docs.title: Keep another phone from taking over
docs.text:
1. On the car’s screen, open its paired devices or phone projection list. Select the comma and set it as the preferred or first device if the car offers that option. For an adapter, use its phone-switching or priority control if available.
  2. On the other Android phone, search Settings for Android Auto. Turn off Wireless Android Auto if the phone offers that switch. If you only want to stop it for this car, disable projection for that phone in the car’s device list. If the car has no separate projection control, remove the other phone’s car or adapter pairing.
  3. Reconnect StarPort with the other phone disconnected. Re-enable the other phone’s Bluetooth afterward if you still use it for calls.

docs.title: Play music from your phone
docs.text:
1. In Galaxy, open Bluetooth → Pair phone or use the companion app. Follow any media-audio pairing prompts.
  2. Open StarPort → Spotify and Phone Audio. Choose Phone over Bluetooth, select your phone, and turn on Phone Audio.
  3. On your phone, select the comma as the media audio output and play music. Calls and microphone audio stay on the phone.

docs.title: Set up Spotify Connect
docs.text:
1. In Spotify and Phone Audio, choose Spotify Connect on the comma. Follow Install under Spotify Soloist to download and upload the ARM64 Linux archive. Keep the archive as downloaded.
  2. With Spotify Premium, use Create Your API Key in Galaxy. Save the key and select Car speakers via StarPort (Android Auto) under Send audio to when prompted.
  3. Start StarPort. Put the phone and comma on the same network for first pairing. Open Spotify on your phone, play something, and select the comma from the device picker. Keep both devices online for playback.

Spotify Connect setup

docs.title: Layout, maps and upkeep
docs.text:
Customize Layout opens the editor for the StarPort display. Offline Road Maps saves road lines for the map overlay.

Wireless projection can interrupt the comma’s usual Wi-Fi connection. Use the Galaxy hotspot for local access. Remote Galaxy still needs Internet on the comma.

If the support certificate expires soon or has expired, use Update or Reinstall under StarPort Support.

docs.title: Start over
docs.text:
For a saved wireless setup, try Reset handshake if Galaxy offers it. This returns to the standard handshake and keeps your Bluetooth pairing.

  • Built-in wireless: In Galaxy, open Tools → Bluetooth, find the car and choose Forget. On the car screen, remove the comma from paired phones or the Android Auto list. Then use Find car again.
  • Wireless adapter: Forget the adapter in Galaxy under Tools → Bluetooth. In the adapter’s own settings, remove the comma if the adapter provides a paired-device list. If it only offers pairing mode, open that mode to pair again. Use the manufacturer’s reset instructions only if stale pairings still block setup. A factory reset clears the adapter’s other saved pairings too.
  • USB or tablet: Return to the matching connection steps. Reconnect the data cable or reconnect the tablet app to the comma’s network.

docs.title: Chestnut (External GPU)
docs.text:
Chestnut is comma.ai’s external GPU dock. The cable, power and software requirements depend on the device.

Learn more from comma.ai: Introducing chestnut · Chestnut shop

docs.title: What does Chestnut do?
docs.text: Chestnut lets the comma run compatible larger models on a desktop GPU.

docs.title: Do I need Chestnut?
docs.text:
Most users do not need Chestnut. Standard driving models can run on the comma’s built-in hardware.

In Galaxy, you can download compatible GPU models for later without Chestnut connected. Running them requires ready, supported hardware. If a selected model needs unavailable hardware, StarPilot can fall back to an eligible model. See Running now in Models to check what is in use.

docs.title: Hardware options
docs.text: Comma sells the dock on its own and a ready-to-drive kit for comma four. Check the Chestnut shop for current kit contents, compatibility and pricing. Comma 3 and 3X setups have their own connection and power requirements.

docs.title: Setup overview
docs.text:
Follow the instructions for your dock, GPU and comma device:

  1. Assemble and secure Chestnut and the compatible GPU.
  2. Connect the specified power supply and data cable for your hardware.
  3. Start StarPilot and check in Models that the hardware is ready and the expected model is running.

Firmware

The device checks that supported firmware is ready before enabling GPU models. If GPU models stay unavailable after connecting Chestnut, ask in Discord.

Driving models

See Models for model selection and hardware requirements, including Jetlink for a supported USB host.

docs.title: Comma Pedal
docs.text:
The Comma Pedal is an interceptor that sits between your accelerator pedal and the car. When assistance is disengaged, your accelerator works normally. When engaged, StarPilot can use the pedal for speed control on supported setups.

On supported non-ACC setups, the pedal can provide acceleration and regen braking in one-pedal mode. On supported ACC-plus-pedal configurations, StarPilot can blend pedal-based regen with ACC friction braking. Standstill behavior depends on the vehicle. See Bolt hardware for specific examples.

You can override assistance with the accelerator. What engages or disengages depends on your vehicle and configuration. See Operation.

docs.title: Pedal Purchase List
docs.text:
Important

This hardware is only necessary if indicated by your car setup guide

  • Comma Pedal
  • Ethernet cable. The pedal supplier recommends round Cat6. Choose a length for the route from your harness box to the accelerator.
  • Optional: DFU Key
    • If the firmware is ever updated, you need a DFU key (or DIY if you are mechanically inclined) to apply new firmware. See the Bolt pedal firmware instructions for details.

Bundle your pedal with a harness box.

If you already have a Harness Cable, but your Harness Box does not have an RJ45 port (or you do not have one), you can bundle your Pedal with a 2x9 or 2x13 pin Harness Box - check your specific cable to ensure you purchase the correct box.

docs.title: Comma Devices
docs.text:
StarPilot supports the Comma 3, Comma 3X, and Comma 4. All three devices provide the cameras, processing, driver monitoring, storage, and vehicle connection needed to run StarPilot. The correct choice mostly depends on what you already own, whether your car uses CAN FD, and whether you want to buy new or used hardware.

Check your car first

A comma device does not connect directly to every car. Check the StarPilot car support page and the comma supported vehicles list before buying anything. Your vehicle may require a specific harness, connector, pedal, or other hardware.

Get $50 off a comma four and support StarPilot

Buying a comma four? Eligible new customers can get $50 off with our comma referral link. We may also receive $50 for a qualifying referral, helping support StarPilot. See comma’s referral terms.

docs.title: Quick comparison
docs.text:
Device Best choice for CAN FD Availability Main difference Comma 4 Most new buyers Built in Available new from comma.ai Much smaller body, improved cooling, and a compact status display Comma 3X Buyers who find a good used unit Built in Usually purchased used Larger touchscreen and the same general performance and camera layout as the Comma 3 Comma 3 Existing owners using StarPilot or another supporting fork Requires a red panda on CAN FD cars End of life and used only No longer supported by stock openpilot

The device does not determine how much steering torque, braking control, or acceleration control your car has. Those capabilities depend on the vehicle and its installed hardware.

docs.title: Comma 4
docs.text:
The Comma 4 is comma.ai's current device and is the recommended option for most people buying new hardware. It uses a Snapdragon 845 MAX, includes 128 GB of storage, supports CAN FD without an additional panda, and has LTE, Wi-Fi, GPS, night-vision driver monitoring, and three cameras.

The Comma 4 provides the same general compute, sensor suite, and functionality as the Comma 3X in a body that comma.ai describes as one-fifth the size. Its cooling system is designed for sustained performance, and its small OLED display is used for status and driving information instead of the large touchscreen found on the Comma 3 and 3X.

Purchase from comma.ai: Comma 4

Mounts

Comma 4 mounts are different from Comma 3 and 3X mounts. If you replace an older device with a Comma 4, install the mount supplied for the Comma 4.

docs.title: Comma 3X
docs.text:
The Comma 3X uses a Snapdragon 845, three 1080p HDR cameras, a 2160 x 1080 OLED touchscreen, 128 GB of storage, LTE, Wi-Fi, GPS, and infrared lighting for driver monitoring. CAN FD support is built in, so it does not require a separate red panda for CAN FD vehicles.

Comma.ai introduced the Comma 3X as a less complex replacement for the Comma 3 with the same general performance and triple-camera system. It remains a good StarPilot device if you already own one or find a used unit in good condition.

Comma.ai now sells the Comma 4 as its current device. Comma 3X units are generally found through the used market or the comma.ai community Discord.

docs.title: Comma 3
docs.text:
The Comma 3 is the oldest of the three devices supported by StarPilot. It uses the same Snapdragon 845 family and triple-camera layout as the Comma 3X, so existing owners can still run current StarPilot releases.

Comma.ai ended official Comma 3 software support on August 26, 2025 to focus on newer hardware. Stock openpilot no longer supports it. StarPilot and some other forks continue to support the Comma 3, but buying one is not advised. Existing owners can continue using it with a supporting fork.

CAN FD vehicles

A Comma 3 requires a red panda to communicate with a CAN FD vehicle. The Comma 3X and Comma 4 have CAN FD support built in. Existing Comma 3 owners should check their vehicle before purchasing a replacement panda.

docs.title: What else do I need?
docs.text:
A typical installation requires:

  • A supported comma device
  • The correct car harness and harness connector
  • A harness box
  • An OBD-C cable
  • A compatible windshield mount

Some StarPilot-supported vehicles need additional hardware, such as a pedal, GM harness, ASCM or SDGM integration, or an OBD-C setup that differs from comma's stock installation. Follow the guide for your specific vehicle rather than ordering from the general list alone.

See the following pages before installation:

  • Car support
  • Installing comma hardware in a Bolt
  • Installing StarPilot
  • OBD-C cable
  • Comma Pedal

docs.title: Buying a used device
docs.text:
Before buying a used Comma 3X, confirm that:

  1. The device boots and reaches its setup screen.
  2. The road and driver-monitoring cameras work and are unobstructed.
  3. The display, USB-C port, Wi-Fi, and GPS work correctly.
  4. The listing includes the correct mount and cable, or you have replacements available.
  5. You know whether your vehicle requires CAN FD.
  6. You can obtain the correct harness and any StarPilot-specific hardware for your car.

Do not assume that a used device includes the correct harness for your vehicle or qualifies for comma.ai warranty service or trade-in credit. The Comma 3 is end-of-life hardware, so buying one is not advised even though StarPilot and some other community forks continue to support it.

docs.title: Optional hardware and services
docs.text:
Use Galaxy on your local network, or pair for remote device management. For phone setup, see Companion Apps. Comma Prime is optional and is not required to run StarPilot.

StarPilot also supports Chestnut for users who want to run larger driving models with an external GPU. Most users do not need Chestnut. See Models for choosing a model and checking its hardware requirements.

docs.title: Which one should I choose?
docs.text:
• Buy a Comma 4 if you want new hardware, built-in CAN FD support, and the smallest current device.
  • Keep using a Comma 3X if you already have one. There is no need to replace a working device solely to run StarPilot.
  • Buying a Comma 3 is not advised. You can keep using one if you already own it and plan to remain on StarPilot or another fork that supports it.

Regardless of the device, you must remain attentive and ready to take control. StarPilot and openpilot are driver-assistance systems, not self-driving systems.

docs.title: GM Harness and Harness Box
docs.text:
Important

This hardware is only necessary if indicated by your car setup guide

The GM harness and harness box are used for openpilot to communicate with your car. This GM harness set is separate from ASCM and SDGM harnesses. Match the harness and box connector before ordering. The supplier currently sells the 9-pin set. Match existing hardware before replacing an individual part.

Purchase from tinybear: Harness set (Harness Cable + Harness Box)

Harness box and pedal compatibility

If your setup calls for a pedal, confirm the box has the required RJ45 port and the correct connector for your harness. See the pedal guide.

docs.title: OBD-C Cable
docs.text:
The comma four comes with a short OBD-C cable. Use an OBD-C cable compatible with your harness and device. Confirm the required connections and length for your setup. ASCM, SDGM, SASCM and OBD harness setups can require different cable lengths. See the Volt and GM hardware guide for examples and the OBD-C schematic for connector details.

Some example options:

  • https://comma.ai/shop/obd-c-cable
  • https://konik.ai/shop/usb-c-cable

docs.title: OBD-II Harness
docs.text:
Important

This hardware is only necessary if indicated by your car setup guide

If your car setup guide calls for an OBD-II harness, check the comma OBD-II Harness.

The Konik OBD2C connector is a development connector for CAN diagnostics with a panda.

Check the connector and what’s included. Confirm the OBD-C cable length required for your car.

docs.title: Installing comma hardware in a Bolt
docs.text:
This page covers Bolt hardware. Follow the comma setup guide for your device and vehicle, alongside the Bolt hardware guide.

Power requirements depend on the harness and vehicle. Follow the guide for your setup. Parked runtime depends on available power, the shutdown timer and the battery-voltage cutoff.

Note

If you are installing a pedal, follow the pedal installation steps before closing up the camera/harness area.

docs.title: Install Video
docs.text:
Hardware and fork options have changed over the years, especially across car variants.

Transport Evolved’s video shows a 2017 Bolt installation. The Ethernet cable is for pedal installations. For software setup, follow Installing StarPilot.

The Stupid White Clip

There is a tiny white clip on the connector to the camera that you have to pull back in order to add the harness. Follow the harness instructions for releasing it.

docs.title: Mounting your Comma
docs.text:
Correct placement gives the road cameras a clear view, keeps driver monitoring aimed at the driver, and leaves room to service the harness and windshield trim later.

Follow the official comma setup guide for your vehicle alongside this page.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Make sure you have:

  • The correct mount for your device
  • The included alcohol wipe or another lint-free alcohol wipe
  • A clean, dry windshield
  • Enough room below the rearview-mirror trim for the device and cable

Use the correct mount

Comma 4 mounts are not compatible with the Comma 3 or 3X. The standard Comma 3X mount works for most windshields, while some steep windshields require the 8-degree Comma 3X mount. Check the comma replacement mounts page if you are unsure.

docs.title: Choose the mounting position
docs.text:
1. Sit in the driver's seat and locate the center of the windshield below the rearview mirror and its trim.
  2. Position the mount as close to the windshield centerline as practical.
  3. Make sure the top of the mount is visible from the driver's seat.
  4. Leave enough space above the device to remove the rearview-mirror trim in the future.
  5. Check that the device will not touch the mirror, trim, or headliner.
  6. Make sure the OBD-C cable can reach the device without being pulled tight or sharply bent.

The device should face straight ahead rather than toward the driver. Do not place it far to one side of the windshield unless your vehicle's layout makes centered placement impossible.

Off-center mounting

Use the recommended physical mounting position and check calibration after moving the device.

docs.title: Attach the mount
docs.text:
1. Remove the comma device from the mount before attaching the mount to the glass.
  2. Clean the selected area with the alcohol wipe.
  3. Let the glass dry completely. Do not touch the cleaned area afterward.
  4. Check the mount's position and orientation one final time.
  5. Peel the cover from the mount's adhesive.
  6. Place the mount on the windshield without sliding it around.
  7. Press firmly in the center, then press outward along the edges so the adhesive makes even contact without bubbles.

Take your time when positioning the mount. The adhesive is difficult to reposition cleanly after it touches the windshield.

docs.title: Attach the device
docs.text:
1. Slide the comma device fully onto the mount.
  2. Confirm that it is seated securely and does not wobble.
  3. Connect the OBD-C cable without placing sideways pressure on the device's port.
  4. Route the cable so it does not block either road camera or the driver-monitoring camera.
  5. Recheck the view from the driver's seat and make sure the device does not interfere with normal visibility.

For a Bolt, see Installing comma hardware in a Bolt for the rest of the harness and cable setup.

docs.title: After mounting
docs.text:
StarPilot may need to calibrate after its first installation or after the device is moved. Park the vehicle before adjusting the mount or removing the device. Never attempt to reposition the device while driving.

If calibration repeatedly fails or the displayed road view appears noticeably tilted, check that:

  • The mount is level and fully attached to the glass.
  • The device is fully seated on the mount.
  • The device faces forward and is not angled toward the driver.
  • The road cameras are not blocked by trim, tint, stickers, or dirt.
  • The correct standard or 8-degree mount is being used for the windshield.

docs.title: Check your calibration with OPCal
docs.text:
OPCal is a community-made tool that reads calibration data from a comma route. It can show where your device's pitch and yaw landed within the allowed range and can scan a drive for invalid calibration messages.

Use Quick look after mounting or moving your device:

  1. Complete a drive long enough for the device to calibrate.
  2. Open comma Connect and select that drive.
  3. Open More info and turn on Public access.
  4. Copy the route name or the URL from your browser.
  5. Open OPCal.
  6. Paste the route name or URL into the input.
  7. Select Quick look to see the first valid calibration and its pitch and yaw position.
  8. Turn off Public access in comma Connect when you are finished.

Use Full scan when calibration became invalid or changed during a drive. Full scan checks the complete route and reports an invalid calibration message along with the most recent valid calibration when one is available.

Public route access

For the public-route method above, enable Public access while reading the route, then turn it off. The processing happens in your browser.

Reading the result

A valid result means the device is within openpilot's accepted calibration limits. It does not necessarily mean the mount is perfectly centered. If the result is close to a limit, the road view is visibly tilted, or calibration repeatedly becomes invalid, inspect the mount before driving again.

OPCal was created by Nelson Chen for the Openpilot Hardware User Group. Thank you to Nelson and the group for building and sharing this helpful tool with the openpilot community. The source code is available in the OPCal GitHub repository.

docs.title: Replacing or moving a mount
docs.text:
If you expect to move or replace the mount, consider buying fresh 3M VHB tape and an electrostatic windshield mounting film. Apply the electrostatic film to the clean windshield, then attach the mount to the film with freshly cut VHB tape. The film keeps the adhesive off the glass and can make the mount easier to remove later.

Choose an electrostatic film that is larger than the mount, trim the VHB tape to fit the mount, and make sure the entire mounting surface is secure before attaching the comma device. Check it periodically for lifting or movement, especially after large temperature changes.

Third-party mounting method

Electrostatic film is a community mounting option and is not part of comma.ai's official installation method. If the film or adhesive does not hold the mount firmly, remove it and use a new official mount directly on the windshield.

Do not reuse damaged adhesive or install a Comma 4 on a Comma 3 or 3X mount.

Remove the device before working on the mount. Take care not to damage windshield tint, heating elements, sensors, or camera equipment near the rearview mirror. If you are unsure how to remove adhesive safely from your windshield, have an automotive glass professional remove it.

docs.title: Installing the Pedal Interceptor
docs.text:
Gen1 Bolt ONLY - Pedal Firmware Update

If you have a Gen 1 Bolt (2017–2021), check the Bolt pedal firmware guide before installation. Confirm with the supplier whether your pedal needs an update and which build to use.

This walkthrough shows a Bolt installation. Connector, cable and trim details differ by vehicle. Follow your hardware guide and turn off the vehicle before working on the connectors.

docs.title: Route the Cable
docs.text: Use the cable type and length recommended for your pedal and vehicle. Follow the vehicle-specific route and secure the cable clear of airbags, moving trim and pedal travel. Leave enough slack at the harness box to refit the cover without pulling on or pinching the cable.

docs.title: Install the Pedal
docs.text:
1. The accelerator has a single cable connected to it. This cable has a red tab that must be pulled back. Then, you can squeeze the connecter to unlatch it, and pull it off.
  2. Connect this cable to the pedal, and push back in the red tab.
  3. Connect the pedal to the accelerator, and push that red tab back in as well.
  4. On most bolts, there is a plastic piece next to the accelerator - the pedal can be tucked up inside this area safely, and this will keep it well out of the way of the accelerator. Alternatively, use a strong adhesive or similar to secure the pedal somewhere safe, where it will not interfere with your pedals.

Warning

It is essential that none of the cable routing or the pedal itself interfere with the normal operation of your brake and accelerator pedals. Ensure that there is no way for these items to tangle, jam, or otherwise block your pedals.

docs.title: Reassembly
docs.text:
You can now re-attach the cover behind the mirror, ensuring no cables get pinched or caught, and replace the small plastic piece at the front. There should be enough space remaining for the USB-C for the comma device and the Ethernet for the pedal to come out.

Verify that the brake and accelerator have full, unobstructed travel before use.

docs.title: Installing StarPilot
docs.text:
The StarPilot install links are:

  • Stable: starpilothq/stable
  • Testing: starpilothq/testing

These are the current working links. The old starpilothq/Dom link still works: its first startup switches the installed branch and update target to testing, including fresh installs made later.

If StarPilot is already installed, see Changing branches.

If your comma is new or already on the setup screen, skip to the instructions for your device.

If openpilot or another fork is already installed:

  1. Park your car and make sure the comma has a good internet connection.
  2. Open Settings > Software.
  3. Select Uninstall and confirm.
  4. Wait for the comma to restart and return to the setup screen.

docs.title: Comma 4
docs.text:
1. Choose Custom Software on the setup screen.
  2. Connect to Wi-Fi when prompted.
  3. Enter starpilothq/stable for Stable or starpilothq/testing for Testing.
  4. Start the installation and let it finish. The comma may restart more than once.

Do not unplug the comma while it is installing or updating AGNOS.

docs.title: Comma 3/3X
docs.text:
1. Connect to Wi-Fi on the setup screen.
  2. Choose to install custom software.
  3. Enter starpilothq/stable for Stable or starpilothq/testing for Testing.
  4. Start the installation and wait for the comma to restart.

You can power the comma inside your home with a suitable USB-C power adapter if the Wi-Fi signal in your car is poor.

docs.title: If You Cannot Open Settings
docs.text:
Use this only if the comma is stuck and you cannot uninstall through Settings > Software.

A factory reset erases stored content and settings on the comma. Download any recordings or logs you need first, if the device is still accessible.

  1. Unplug the comma and wait 60 seconds.
  2. Plug it back in and immediately tap the screen repeatedly until the reset prompt appears.
  3. On comma 4, tap reset & erase, then swipe to confirm. On comma 3/3X, follow the Confirm prompts.
  4. After it returns to setup, follow the instructions above for your device.

Recommended settings page

See the settings page

Stuck on the boot logo after installing?

See the faq

Other install issues

Message us in Discord or flash your comma and retry. Make sure you try the steps above multiple times before resorting to flashing.

Want to change settings from your phone?

Use the Galaxy

docs.title: Branches
docs.text:
StarPilot currently has two main channels:

Branch Purpose Stability stable Stable releases. Use this unless you have a specific reason not to. Stable. Recommended for everyone. testing The active testing branch. Changes are made to it regularly and it may break at any time. Commonly used by users who want to test new features or fixes that are still in development. Unstable. Use at your own risk.

docs.title: Channel names and the one-time migration
docs.text:
The testing channel is now testing, formerly Dom. Dom remains a compatibility bridge for existing devices and old install links; future updates and development continue on testing.

The stable channel is stable, formerly StarPilot. The old StarPilot install link and update channel also move once to stable. This naming change keeps version 6.7.9; it does not upgrade to the rebase. dev is reserved for the maintainer’s personal work, not a recommended user channel.

The migration release keeps the installed software version and settings. It changes the local branch and update target once; it does not install the rebase, erase recordings, remove models, reset calibration, or unpair Galaxy. A later deliberate branch switch is respected and does not run a chain of renames.

Update normally while parked. After the migration release starts, Galaxy’s installed branch and update target show stable for old StarPilot installs, or testing for old Dom installs. Devices can complete this local rename without a network connection after downloading the release.

The old StarPilot and Dom links remain available for devices that update later. GitHub does not redirect branch names; these preserved compatibility releases perform the one-time switch locally.

docs.title: Using Galaxy (Recommended)
docs.text:
Park and turn off the vehicle; keep the comma powered and online. In Galaxy, open Tools → System Tools → Software & Updates. Under Advanced options → Branch, choose Stable or Testing.

To update to the latest version of a branch:

  1. Select Update. Confirm Update & restart, or Restart & install if the update is already prepared.
  2. If an update was installed, wait for the device to restart and Galaxy to reconnect. An up-to-date branch needs no restart.

If Galaxy cannot verify the update after five minutes, check the connection and the installed version before trying again.

To choose a specific version instead:

  1. Select a version from the list.
  2. Choose Install selected version or Download and install selected version.
  3. Confirm the restart and wait for Galaxy to reconnect.

Choosing a branch or version does not install it. Download only prepares a version for later installation.

docs.title: Direct on device
docs.text:
With the vehicle off and comma powered and online, open Settings → Software. If Target Branch is shown, select stable or testing. Otherwise, choose the branch in Galaxy.

On the Comma 3/3X interface:

  1. Use CHECK, then DOWNLOAD when offered.
  2. Wait for the download to finish.
  3. Select Install Update → INSTALL and wait for the device to restart.

On the Comma 4 interface:

  1. Use check for update, then download update when offered.
  2. Wait for the download to finish.
  3. Select install now and wait for the device to restart.

docs.title: Automatic updates
docs.text: Download updates automatically prepares updates while the vehicle is off. Install updates automatically restarts the device on the configured schedule, only while the vehicle is off. These are separate settings. Configure the Automatic restart schedule and its time zone under Advanced options in Galaxy.

docs.title: Returning to the previous version
docs.text:
In Galaxy, choose Select previous version, then Install selected version, and confirm Restore previous version. Restoring turns off automatic downloads.

Fast Update and previous-version restore depend on compatible saved software and the installed operating system. If the updater requires a full update, use the normal download/install path instead.

docs.title: Galaxy & Features
docs.text: Galaxy is StarPilot’s browser interface for settings, models, routes, and device tools. Feature availability depends on your car and hardware. Read Operation for driving behavior.

docs.title: Companion apps
docs.text:
The iOS and Android apps can connect over Galaxy Wi-Fi or a shared network. Bluetooth supports basic controls. Recordings and replay require Galaxy Wi-Fi or LAN.

See Companion Apps for downloads, pairing, source repositories and beta access.

docs.title: Local access
docs.text:
Put your phone or computer and comma on the same Wi-Fi or Ethernet network. On the comma, open Settings → Device → Galaxy or Pair with Galaxy.

Scan the local QR code or open http://<comma-ip>:8082/. Galaxy Access & Install → Local access also lists the address. Direct local access needs no Galaxy password.

docs.title: Remote access
docs.text:
While parked, choose Set password & pair or Pair with Galaxy on the comma, or Pair in local Galaxy Access & Install. Choose a new password of at least eight characters.

The separate remote QR code opens your device-specific galaxy.firestar.link address. Save it and sign in with your password. Remote access requires Internet and the Galaxy tunnel, which may take a few minutes to connect. Bookmark each device’s link separately.

docs.title: Unpairing
docs.text:
To stop remote access, choose Unpair remote Galaxy on the comma or Unpair in local Galaxy. The old remote link stops working; local access remains available. Pair again for a new remote link.

Keep your password and App key private. The App key grants remote access.

docs.title: Installed web app and hotspot
docs.text:
Open your remote Galaxy link and choose Install web app or your browser’s Add to Home Screen. This web app uses the remote link and needs Internet.

For local access without Internet, enable Galaxy Wi-Fi Hotspot while parked, set its password, then open http://172.31.254.1:8082/. The hotspot provides local access; it does not share Internet.

docs.title: Main
docs.text: Home shows device status, drive totals and recent drives. Toggles lets you search or browse settings; follow each change’s save or confirmation prompts. Some changes require Park. Tools opens the device tools.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text: In local Galaxy, Routes lists saved drives. Open one and choose Footage for camera video or Replay with UI for the driving screen. Replay needs saved driving logs and road video for the segment. Export segment saves one replay clip. Export route combines replayable clips and skips missing ranges.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
See this in Galaxy: the Tools menu

Tap Tools in the bottom navigation, then choose a feature card. Scroll for more tools.

The bottom navigation stays within reach on a phone. Tap the image to open it full size.

Tool Purpose Bluetooth Pair devices, manage audio and map controller buttons Cameras & Monitoring Camera previews, Sentry and visual monitoring Colors & Layout Customize widgets, colors and road views Logs & Diagnostics Inspect crashes, device status and support logs Models Single models, model pairs, downloads and Jetlink Navigation & Maps Routes, saved places and offline map data Tuning and Analysis FLM Auto Learn results and live plots StarPort Car-screen display, layout and audio System Tools Software updates, version history and switching between Stable and Testing Galaxy Access & Install Remote pairing, app installation and hotspot

Vehicle identification is under Toggles → Vehicle.

docs.title: Features at a glance
docs.text: Feature What you can do Requirements and limits Galaxy Manage settings, models, software, logs, and recordings from a browser. Local access uses your network; remote access requires pairing and Internet. Driving models Choose a single model or a steering/speed model pair. Model availability depends on hardware; some need Chestnut. Navigation Set destinations in Galaxy and give the model route guidance. Requires a Mapbox key and Navigation enabled in Galaxy. The driver remains responsible for turns and exits. Lane Centering Bias the model's path toward the center of detected lane lines. Experimental; falls back to the normal model path when conditions are unsuitable. Speed Limit Controller Configure speed-limit sources, offsets, confirmation, and overrides. Source availability varies, and reported limits can be wrong. Sentry Mode Review images captured after sustained movement while parked. Experimental; uses the device accelerometer and requires the device to remain powered. Bluetooth controls Pair audio devices and map Bluetooth or USB controller buttons to Quick Select and driving screen actions. Experimental; configure Controller Buttons in local Galaxy with the vehicle off.

docs.title: Galaxy tuning and support
docs.text:
Galaxy’s tuning tools include live plots, lateral tuning, and a view of settings that differ from defaults. These help you describe a problem when opening a support ticket.

For connection and pairing instructions, see Access Galaxy.

docs.title: Driving models and optional Chestnut support
docs.text:
Use Models for Single model, Model pair (formerly Model Laboratory), downloads, and Jetlink. Most models run on the comma itself; Big models need compatible external hardware.

You can download GPU models for later without Chestnut connected. Model selections take effect the next time the driving model starts.

docs.title: Navigation through Galaxy
docs.text:
Search for a destination, compare routes, and save favorites in Galaxy. StarPilot sends route information to the comma device, displays turn instructions, and provides upcoming maneuver information to the driving model. Turn guidance is limited to supported low-speed turns with the matching turn signal on and the corresponding blindspot clear. Route guidance can also help slow for upcoming maneuvers when StarPilot controls speed.

In Galaxy, open Tools → Navigation & Maps → Setup. Add a Mapbox key and turn on Navigation. An optional Google key adds Google maps, routing, and place search alongside Mapbox. Navigation is a driving aid: it does not guarantee the car will complete a route or make an exit.

Configure navigation and learn how route guidance works.

docs.title: Steering, speed, and driving preferences
docs.text:
StarPilot offers settings for lateral tuning, driving personalities, curve speed control, and Driving Mode choices of Automatic, Chill, and Experimental. Automatic switches between Chill and Experimental using your saved conditions. Availability and behavior depend on your vehicle's steering and longitudinal capabilities.

The experimental Lane Centering feature adjusts the model's path using detected lane lines when conditions allow. Its settings include Lane offset, Model path preference, Lane Centering Strength, and Pause on signal. This particular feature is separate from the general lane-centering assistance provided by openpilot.

Speed Limit Controller can use map data, supported dashboard limits, and optional camera-based sign detection. You can require confirmation before applying a new limit, set offsets, and configure overrides. It can cap speed below your cruise SET speed; accepting a limit normally does not change SET.

On supported configurations, Use StarPilot Longitudinal Planner selects the planner for the next drive. Enhanced Stops improves stopping at traffic lights and enables stopping at detected stop signs. See Operation for how the hold releases.

Start with the settings guide, then read the operation guide for the behavior and limitations of driving controls.

docs.title: Sentry Mode and Bluetooth accessories
docs.text:
Sentry Mode detects sustained movement through the comma device's accelerometer while parked and captures camera images. Galaxy provides event history, sensitivity settings, and notification options. It is motion-triggered event capture; it does not continuously watch camera video for every person passing the car.

Bluetooth support is available on comma 3, 3X, and 4 for audio and controller input. Galaxy provides pairing and Controller Buttons mapping for Bluetooth or USB controllers. Bluetooth management is also available on the comma device. Both Sentry Mode and Bluetooth are documented as experimental.

Set up Sentry Mode or pair Bluetooth accessories.

docs.title: Supported devices and cars
docs.text:
