StarPilot supports comma 3, 3X, and 4, but device support does not establish compatibility with a particular car. The vehicle's year, trim, steering system, ACC configuration, and installed harness or pedal determine which controls are available.

StarPilot's vehicle work extends beyond GM. The compatibility guide lists additions and improvements across multiple manufacturers, while the car guides explain specific hardware setups.

  • Compare comma devices.
  • Check vehicle compatibility.
  • Find car setup guides.
  • Install StarPilot.

docs.title: Shared work and project development
docs.text:
StarPilot builds on openpilot and work from the wider community. Features such as Always On Lateral, Conditional Experimental Mode, themes, and Speed Limit Controller have shared project history; their presence alone does not make them exclusive to StarPilot. The StarPilot project README describes the project's features.

For questions about a feature on your car or software branch, use the StarPilot support channels. StarPilot remains driver assistance and requires an attentive driver ready to take control.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Open Galaxy → Tools → Models to choose driving models and manage downloads.

The driving model processes camera video and plans steering and acceleration or braking. Preferences vary with your car, roads, region and conditions. Use the current catalog and community favorites, and ask for feedback in Discord.

docs.title: Single model
docs.text:
See this in Galaxy: model selection and status

Open Tools → Models. The active Small and Big selections appear above Model Randomizer, Running now, and Jetlink.

This parked example reports “No running model.” The model names and selections shown are examples, not recommendations. Tap the image to open it full size.

Active Small · On-device runs on the comma’s built-in compute. Active Big · External selects a larger model for compatible external hardware. Choose None — always use Active Small to stay with the on-device model.

Chestnut is supported on comma 3, 3X and 4. You can download a Big model before connecting it. Without an external GPU or an active Jetlink host, Active Small is used and your Big selection stays saved.

Selections take effect the next time the driving model starts. Running now reports the loaded model.

docs.title: Model Randomizer
docs.text: Model Randomizer chooses among eligible installed, verified models at each start, trying a different model when another is available. Use Include in Randomizer to exclude individual models. Favorites do not change the random pool.

docs.title: Model pair
docs.text:
Model pair combines one model’s Lateral model—steering and path—with another’s Longitudinal model—speed and lead pacing.

  1. Turn off the vehicle. Connect a firmware-ready Chestnut; the pair runtime must also be available.
  2. Use Show pairable models and download the indicated pair variants. Ordinary on-device downloads alone do not establish readiness.
  3. Choose Model pair, then two different downloaded models for the lateral and longitudinal roles. Valid selections save automatically and apply when the driving model next starts.
  4. Check Running now and the pair status.

At least one model must have a Chestnut variant. Two Big models cannot run together; use a Small model for at least one role. Pairing increases inference time and can cause model-lag warnings.

Your Small and Big fallback selections remain saved. Choose Single model to return to them at the next start.

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text: Browse On the comma, Needs GPU or Jetlink, or All. Search, filter favorites or pairable models, and sort by release date, name or size. Download individual models or use Download all. Progress and retry controls appear here. Park before downloading.

docs.title: Jetlink
docs.text:
Jetlink requires a comma 3X or comma 4. Under Jetlink → Remote model connection, choose USB computer or iPhone / iPad. Set up while parked with a USB 3 data cable and separate power. Keep the computer awake, or the iPhone app open and unlocked. Jetlink stays off while Chestnut is connected. Disconnect wired Android Auto before enabling Jetlink.

Jetlink runs Active Big on its host, which downloads the model itself. Prepared means the remote model is built, rather than active. Local Small remains available, and your Small and Chestnut selections stay saved.

Follow the Jetlink host setup guide.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
Openpilot is driver assistance, not self-driving. It performs best on highways.

On supported configurations, it provides adaptive cruise control and automated lane centering. Traffic-light and stop-sign behavior depends on the driving mode, planner, Enhanced Stops and vehicle. Curves and low-speed turns are limited by the vehicle’s steering capabilities.

You must stay attentive and ready to steer or brake. Driver monitoring helps check your attention.

docs.title: Basic Operation
docs.text:
1. Pay attention at all times. You are responsible for your vehicle’s operation.
  2. You can steer, accelerate, brake, or disengage openpilot at any time.
  3. Use your vehicle’s engagement controls; steering and speed can engage separately.
  4. Button and pedal behavior depends on the vehicle and AOL settings. Manual steering or accelerator input may override assistance without disengaging it.
  5. To adjust openpilot max speed, use the CC +/- buttons. Depending on the car, your dash may not reflect the max speed, so instead use the openpilot UI’s max speed shown.

docs.title: Always On Lateral
docs.text:
With Always On Lateral (AOL), steering assistance can remain active when cruise speed control is disengaged. AOL can be armed (ready to assist), active or paused. Pedal and Cancel/OFF behavior depends on the vehicle and settings. You can still override steering manually. Use the controls for your vehicle to enable or disable AOL.

To permanently disable, see settings.

docs.title: Lane Changes
docs.text:
1. Verify it is safe to change lanes.
  2. Turn on blinker.
  3. Nudge the steering wheel to initiate the lane change.

Check your blind spot!

Openpilot will attempt to use your blind spot monitors on supported cars, but you should always check yourself.

Lane-change assistance depends on the minimum-speed setting and vehicle capabilities.

Nudge-less lane changes

Step 3 can be skipped when Automatic Lane Changes is enabled, after the configured delay and when lane and blindspot checks allow. If Require Cruise for Automatic Lane Changes is enabled, engage factory cruise or StarPilot speed control before signaling. Narrower or uncertain lanes still require a nudge.

Be careful if you use this non-recommended setting.

docs.title: Border Colors
docs.text:
Color Meaning Dark blue No active StarPilot steering or speed assistance Dark teal AOL armed and waiting to assist Teal Steering assistance without active speed control Pink StarPilot speed control only Green Steering and speed assistance together, or steering with factory cruise Yellow Manually selected Chill mode Orange Experimental or stop-related state Red Traffic Mode Purple Switchback Mode Grey Manual steering or speed override

Mode and override colors can take precedence over the steering/speed colors. Alerts and optional turn-signal or blindspot edge indicators can also change the displayed border.

docs.title: Max Speed
docs.text: Your cruise SET speed is shown in the driving UI; its position depends on the layout. SET is the driver’s cruise ceiling. Speed-limit control, curve-speed control or the active planner can request a lower speed.

docs.title: Speed Limit Controller
docs.text:
The Speed Limit Controller (SLC) can use map data, dashboard speed limits or camera-detected signs, depending on your configuration.

When StarPilot controls speed, SLC can limit the target to the accepted speed limit plus your configured offset, up to your cruise SET speed. Accepting a limit normally does not change SET.

The driving display shows the speed-limit sign and optional offset. Status text explains whether SLC is using the speed limit, using SET, awaiting confirmation or being overridden.

See the Speed Limit Controller guide for source, offset, confirmation, and override settings.

docs.title: Submitting New Speed Limits
docs.text: If you see an incorrect or missing map-based speed limit, submit an edit to OpenStreetMap. The correction reaches StarPilot after it appears in newer map data and your device uses that coverage. See Speed Limit Maps to download updated coverage for your region.

docs.title: Vision Speed Limit Detection
docs.text:
StarPilot can read speed limit signs with the road camera as an SLC source. See the Vision speed limits guide for setup and accuracy guidance.

In Galaxy, open Toggles → Longitudinal (Speed & Following) → Speed Limit Controller. Select Vision under Primary source, Secondary source or Third source, where available.

Show speed limit signs controls the display. Enable Speed Limit Controller for accepted limits to affect speed on supported configurations.

docs.title: Help us improve it
docs.text:
The model gets better with more real-world driving data. If you'd like to help:

  1. Select Vision as a speed-limit source in Toggles → Longitudinal (Speed & Following) → Speed Limit Controller.
  2. If you also use Maps as a source, install map data for your region.
  3. Drive as normal.
  4. In Comma Connect, open the route, choose Files -> Upload All Files, then under More Info enable Public Access and copy the route ID.
  5. Submit the route through the vision speed limit submission form.

Let your uploads finish

Make sure all files finish uploading before turning the device off or disconnecting from Wi-Fi/hotspot. You can confirm in Comma Connect that rlog.zst and fcamera.hevc are present for every segment.

docs.title: Curve Speed Controller
docs.text:
The Curve Speed Controller (CSC) uses learned cornering preferences to reduce speed for curves when StarPilot controls acceleration and braking on supported configurations.

With Show Curve status enabled, the display can show CURVE with its speed target, or CURVE LEARNING with learning progress.

With CSC enabled on a supported configuration, it can learn on qualifying curves while you control speed yourself, with no lead vehicle tracked and no turn signal active. Qualifying accelerator or brake feedback during a CSC-controlled curve can also adjust saved preferences.

docs.title: Longitudinal Planner and Enhanced Stops
docs.text:
Use StarPilot Longitudinal Planner selects the planner for the next drive.

On supported configurations, Enhanced Stops improves stopping behavior at traffic lights and enables stopping at detected stop signs. Release behavior depends on the stop and the vehicle. If Enhanced Stops is holding the vehicle, press the accelerator to continue when it’s safe.

On builds that expose Always Hold Enhanced Stops in developer settings, an acquired hold waits for Resume or accelerator input while assistance is active and the required inputs are valid. Disengaging assistance or losing required data can end the hold. Be ready to hold the vehicle with the brake. This option applies on the next drive.

docs.title: Experimental Mode
docs.text:
Driving Mode offers Automatic, Chill and Experimental.

Experimental mode, also known as end-to-end longitudinal (e2e long), lets the driving model influence acceleration and braking on supported configurations. The active planner and vehicle limits still apply.

Behavior varies with the driving model and conditions. It may brake or accelerate unexpectedly; stay attentive and ready to take control.

docs.title: Conditional Experimental Mode
docs.text: Conditional Experimental Mode (CEM) is presented as Automatic in Driving Mode. It switches between Chill and Experimental using your saved conditions. Configure these under Automatic conditions.

docs.title: CEM Widgets and Meaning
docs.text: The on-screen indicator shows the reason for the current mode choice, such as speed, a lead vehicle, curves, a turn signal or a stop condition.

docs.title: Conditional Chill Mode
docs.text: Older saved Conditional Chill Mode (CCM) selections are handled as Automatic. Current settings use Driving Mode and Automatic conditions, rather than a separate CCM editor.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
Navigation displays a route and can help the driving model prepare for turns. It does not drive to the destination for you. Stay ready to steer, especially at intersections and exits. See Navigation & Maps for setup.

On supported configurations, Turn Signal Guidance can help the model choose a turning path at low speed even without a route. Steering assistance must be active. See Lateral Tuning for the setting.

docs.title: Configure Settings
docs.text:
The default settings are good for most users and are recommended. Saved settings may carry between compatible versions, but compatibility across branches and other forks is not guaranteed. Use Galaxy’s Toggle backup to save editable toggles, layout and colors before switching software.

The below sections highlight settings that might be worth looking at. If you have trouble finding any settings, use Galaxy's toggle search.

See this in Galaxy: browse settings

Tap Toggles, choose a category, then tap Manage beside the group you need.

Categories sit above the settings groups in portrait view. Tap the image to open it full size.

See this in Galaxy: find a setting with search

Tap the search icon and type a feature name. Each result shows its settings category; choose the matching result to open that page.

Search helps when you know the feature name but not its category. Tap the image to open it full size.

If behavior feels off or the car drives unexpectedly, try resetting your toggles to default or using safe mode.

Changing tuning values

If you’re going to change a value, make small changes within the setting’s allowed range. Change one setting at a time and follow vehicle-specific guidance.

Want to change settings from your phone?

Use the Galaxy

Follow each setting’s apply-timing note. A saved choice may take effect on the next drive or after a restart.

docs.title: Safe Mode
docs.text: Safe Mode temporarily bypasses the custom features and tuning that support it, without erasing their saved settings. This can help check whether a custom setting is contributing to unexpected behavior. Its effects depend on the vehicle and feature. Follow any restart prompt.

docs.title: Openpilot Toggles
docs.text:
Enable openpilot to use driver assistance. Speed-control options depend on your vehicle and setup; follow the guide for your exact configuration.

Alpha Longitudinal may appear as openpilot Longitudinal Control (Alpha). Where available, it requests StarPilot acceleration and braking control for the next drive and may disable factory Automatic Emergency Braking.

When factory ACC controls speed, StarPilot’s SLC, CSC and Enhanced Stops cannot control speed.

docs.title: Sounds & Alerts
docs.text:
Under Sounds & Alerts, use Engagement Chime and Disengagement Alert to adjust those sounds. Immediate Warning and Soft Warning retain minimum volume limits.

We do not recommend changing the volume of any important alerts.

Green Light Alert chimes when the model’s traffic-light stop prediction clears while you remain stopped. Lead Departing Alert chimes when the tracked vehicle ahead starts moving while you remain stopped.

docs.title: Driving Mode and Automatic conditions
docs.text:
Driving Mode offers Automatic, Chill and Experimental. Automatic switches between Chill and Experimental using your saved conditions.

Open Automatic conditions to configure conditions involving speed, curves, lead vehicles, turn signals and stop lights. Model stop time currently defaults to 7.7 seconds. Start with the default and check why Automatic activates before adjusting it.

Read more about CEM in the operation guide.

docs.title: Conditional Chill Mode
docs.text: Older saved CCM selections are handled as Automatic; current controls use Driving Mode and Automatic conditions. Read more about CCM in the operation guide.

docs.title: Curve Speed Control
docs.text: Read more about CSC in the operation guide

docs.title: Customize Driving Personalities
docs.text:
Custom Following and Jerk enables saved following-distance and jerk settings for the driving personalities. Acceleration and deceleration profile selections apply independently.

Switch personalities using the supported following-distance button, on-screen personality widget or Cycle Driving Personality in Quick Select.

For optional Bluetooth or USB controller setup, see the Bluetooth guide.

docs.title: Extra stopped-lead distance
docs.text:
Extra stopped-lead distance adds space behind slow or stopped lead vehicles with the StarPilot planner. Zero keeps the normal gap.

This adjusts the gap, not whether StarPilot detects a lead or begins braking in time.

docs.title: Wheel Controls
docs.text:
Under Wheel Controls, Short press and Hold configure speed increments where StarPilot controls cruise SET.

On compatible Toyota setups, Swap Toyota Cruise Steps makes a short press change SET by 5 and a hold by 1, in the selected speed units. Factory cruise-button behavior depends on the vehicle.

docs.title: Always on Lateral
docs.text:
Under Lateral (Steering) → Always On Lateral, Enable Always On Lateral keeps steering assistance available independently of cruise speed control.

Available controls include Brake pause below. Button and pedal behavior depends on your vehicle and settings. See the Operation guide for armed, active and paused behavior.

docs.title: Lane Changes
docs.text:
Automatic Lane Changes: Recommended Off. With this off, nudge the steering wheel after signaling to begin an assisted lane change.

Allow lane changes and Minimum lane-change speed govern availability. Automatic changes use the configured delay and lane/blindspot checks. If Require Cruise for Automatic Lane Changes is enabled, engage cruise before signaling.

Stay Aware while Changing Lanes

Always check your blind spot yourself. Detection depends on the vehicle and available sensor information.

docs.title: Lateral Tuning
docs.text:
Where supported, Steering Controller offers Stock Controller and StarPilot Controller. Controller changes apply on the next drive.

Under Steering and Torque, Turn Signal Guidance uses your turn signal to help the model choose a turning path at low speeds on supported configurations.

Use StarPilot Auto Learn uses data from your drives to refine torque profiles. On current testing builds, moving a manual slider locks that setting while Auto Learn can continue on the others. Select Default to unlock the setting.

While parked with Auto Learn enabled, Accept finding in StarPilot Tuner saves an eligible finding for the next drive and lets Auto Learn keep refining it. Check Applied now to see what the controller is using.

See this in Galaxy: manual tuning and Auto Learn

On supported vehicles, open Tools → Tuning and Analysis → Your tune, then find Steering balance under Explore your settings.

Moving a slider can lock that setting; viewing it does not. This example excludes vehicle details and recorded-drive findings. Do not copy its values as a tune for your car. Tap the image to open it full size.

For a Discord tuning request, Prep My Vehicle for Tuning prepares supported steering settings before recording a route. Turn it off afterward to restore your previous tuning preferences.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Open Galaxy → Tools → Navigation & Maps → Setup, enable Navigation, and save a public Mapbox token. See Navigation & Maps for routes, GPS, and offline maps.

docs.title: Backup and reset
docs.text:
In Galaxy’s Toggle backup, use Back up toggles to save editable toggles, driving-screen layout and colors.

Use Restore toggles while parked, with the same metric/imperial units as the backup. Compatible settings are restored; unavailable settings are skipped.

Review the result after restoring. A change in the session, vehicle, or parked state can stop a restore partway through. If the restore stops early or the layout fails to restore, check your current toggles and layout before trying again.

Reset toggles to default lets you review the changes before confirming while parked. Calibration, downloaded models, accounts and network credentials are kept. Settings unavailable for the vehicle remain unchanged.

docs.title: Companion Apps
docs.text:
Use a companion app to access Galaxy from your phone. Available tools depend on your app, connection and StarPilot build.

  • iOS — StarPilot BT by natehuby76.
  • Android — Galaxy by dirwin31.

docs.title: Pair your phone
docs.text:
While parked, open Settings → Bluetooth → Pair phone on the comma, then follow the pairing prompts in your companion app. If the pairing window has closed, open it again on the comma.

Phone pairing is separate from pairing an audio accessory or controller or setting up remote access in the browser.

docs.title: Choose a connection
docs.text:
Bluetooth-only access supports basic controls and settings where available. Use Galaxy Wi-Fi or the same local network for camera images, recordings, replay and larger transfers. See Local access in Galaxy for browser-based setup.

For beta access and help trying new test features, ask in Discord.

docs.title: Galaxy for Android
docs.text: Galaxy for Android brings Galaxy to your phone through local Wi-Fi, remote access or Bluetooth. Download Galaxy on Google Play. Maintained by dirwin31. Source repository.

docs.title: Set up Galaxy
docs.text:
1. Install the app and use a compatible StarPilot build on your comma.
  2. While parked, join Galaxy Wi-Fi or the same local network as your comma. Open Galaxy and choose Wi-Fi & LAN in Connections.
  3. To use Bluetooth later, open Connections → Add Bluetooth Phone Pairing and follow the Add pairing prompts. Allow nearby-device access when Android asks. If the app can’t open pairing over Wi-Fi, open Settings → Bluetooth → Pair phone on the comma and try again.
  4. Load Galaxy over Wi-Fi if the app says it needs a Wi-Fi visit before Bluetooth can open the saved screens.

docs.title: Choose a connection
docs.text: Connection When to use it Automatic Tries Wi-Fi and LAN first, then Remote if configured, then a saved Bluetooth connection. Wi-Fi & LAN Use Galaxy Wi-Fi or a shared network for camera images, recordings, replay and downloads. Remote Reach your comma over the Internet when away from the local network. Set up remote Galaxy first. Sign in using your Galaxy ID or add the App key from Galaxy Access. Keep the App key private. Bluetooth Use supported settings and basic controls near your paired comma. Switch to Wi-Fi or LAN for media and direct downloads.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
• Manage settings and routes. Open Galaxy to configure the comma or review Routes over a supported connection. Choose No StarPilot? Explore the demo on the connection screen to try the interface with sample data.
  • Share phone GPS. In Connections → Phone GPS, select Share phone GPS with StarPilot and allow location access. Location updates reach your comma over Bluetooth or local Wi-Fi. Keep the Phone GPS notification active while sharing. See Position / GPS for the choices on the comma.
  • Get Sentry alerts. Allow Android notifications and enable Galaxy App Alerts where available in Sentry. Test alert delivery after setup. Delivery depends on the app build and configured notification service.
  • Share a destination. Share a supported Google Maps place to Galaxy to open it in Navigation & Maps.
  • Set up Bluetooth music. If Set up music only appears in Connections, follow its prompts to add music pairing while keeping your app pairing.

docs.title: Connection problems
docs.text: Check the connection mode, comma power and Android permissions. For an expired Bluetooth pairing, use Forget pairing on this phone, clear the matching saved pairing on the comma, then open Pair phone and pair again. For a remote error, confirm both devices have Internet and check that the Galaxy ID or App key matches your paired comma.

docs.title: Try a beta build
docs.text:
With the same Google account you use for Google Play, join the Android beta group, then open Google Play testing and choose Become a tester.

Newer testing builds can share destinations from Google Maps or Waze directly to StarPilot, restrict automatic LAN discovery to preferred Wi-Fi networks, and save supported toggle changes to sync on reconnect.

docs.title: Report a problem through Discord
docs.text:
If your build shows Connections → Debugging options → Report a problem, use it to send app diagnostics to support.

  1. Select Connect with Discord and sign in.
  2. Describe the problem. Choose New support thread or an existing thread for a follow-up.
  3. Tap Send report. After it sends, use Open Discord thread to follow replies.

Your description and Discord identity are visible in the support forum. Diagnostics go to a private support channel. If your build does not show this option, use the Ticket System.

For beta access and help trying new test features, ask in Discord.

docs.title: StarPilot BT for iOS
docs.text:
StarPilot BT brings Galaxy to your iPhone. Download StarPilot BT on the App Store. Maintained by natehuby76. Source repository.

Controls and features can vary with the installed app and StarPilot build.

docs.title: Set up StarPilot BT
docs.text:
1. Install the app on an iPhone running iOS 17 or later. Your comma needs a compatible StarPilot build with the Bluetooth bridge. Initial bridge setup needs Internet access on the comma.
  2. While parked, join the same Wi-Fi network as your comma or join its Galaxy hotspot. Open StarPilot BT and allow Local Network and Bluetooth when prompted.
  3. Under Your comma, connect on Local Wi-Fi and select your device if more than one appears. Let the app load Galaxy from your comma.
  4. To set up Bluetooth for later, choose Bluetooth and tap Set up Bluetooth. The app opens the pairing window on your comma and saves the pairing. If your app asks you to open Pair phone first, use Settings → Bluetooth → Pair phone on the comma and follow the prompts in the app.

docs.title: Choose a connection
docs.text: Connection When to use it Automatic Tries Local Wi-Fi, Tunnel and Bluetooth in that order by default. Use Set order to change the priority. Local Wi-Fi Connect over Galaxy Wi-Fi or a shared network. Use this for recordings, camera images and network tools. Bluetooth Use supported settings and basic controls close to your paired comma, even without Wi-Fi. Open Galaxy over a network connection first so the app can save its screens.

docs.title: Set up the Galaxy tunnel
docs.text: If your build shows Galaxy tunnel, connect to your comma over Local Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, then tap Set up next to it in Settings. Scan the remote Galaxy QR code on the comma or paste its private Galaxy link. Sign in and tap Use tunnel. Both devices need Internet for Tunnel. See Remote access to pair your device for remote access first.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
• Manage settings and update Galaxy screens. Open Galaxy to view toggles and device information. Under Settings → Galaxy screens, tap Check for updates. Use Local Wi-Fi or Tunnel to download them.
  • Review footage and logs. Use Local Wi-Fi for Routes, camera images and downloads. Use the iOS share sheet to save or share a downloaded file.
  • Share a destination. From a supported maps app, share a place to StarPilot. If the comma is unreachable, the app can save the destination to send when it reconnects.
  • Share phone location. Turn on Share phone location in Settings and follow the iOS permission prompts. In Navigation & Maps, choose how StarPilot uses the phone’s position.
  • Get Sentry phone alerts. Turn on Sentry phone alerts in Settings and allow notifications. When the phone is registered and alerts are configured, use Advanced connection options → Test Sentry alerts → Test to check delivery. See Sentry Mode.
  • Play phone music. While connected, tap Set up next to Phone music. Pair from the iPhone’s Bluetooth settings and select the comma as an audio output in Control Center.

docs.title: Connection problems
docs.text: Keep the comma powered and nearby. Check the app’s Bluetooth or Local Network permission for the route you selected. If the app can no longer verify the saved pairing, follow its reconnect prompt.

docs.title: Submit logs through Discord
docs.text:
1. Open Settings → Logs & support → Report a problem on Discord. If the app can’t connect to your comma, use Submit connection log on the connection screen instead.
  2. Tap Connect Discord if prompted and sign in. The phone needs Internet to submit the report.
  3. Describe what happened and what you tried. Review the attached diagnostics, then tap Send. The app captures fresh diagnostics and the installed app version.
  4. Choose New thread for a new problem or select an existing report for a follow-up. Tap Send report and open the Discord thread to see replies.

Your description and Discord username appear in the support forum. Diagnostics, which can include device names and local network addresses, go to the private support channel. To save a copy separately, use Logs & support → Troubleshooting → Export logs (.txt).

For beta access and help trying new test features, ask in Discord.
